exhibitions.title: Luminous Color
exhibitions.description: Nineteenth-century oil sketches from the Thaw Collection exploring how artists captured light and luminosity through color.

exhibitions.title: Common Sense
exhibitions.description: An exhibition that puts America's past in dialogue with its present.
exhibitions.venue_address: 200 Eastern Parkway, Brooklyn, NY 11238, United States

exhibitions.title: Splendido, As Seen by Chris Rhodes
exhibitions.description: Twenty-seven photographs by Chris Rhodes of Belmond's Hotel Splendido above Portofino, from its interiors and landscape to its staff and guests.
exhibitions.venue_address: 380 Columbus Avenue at West 78th Street, New York, NY 10024

exhibitions.title: Modernity and Opulence: Women of the Wiener Werkstätte
Pierre Huyghe: UUmwelt
exhibitions.description: Freestanding screens throughout the Abby Aldrich Rockefeller Sculpture Garden use machine learning and fMRI-derived data to generate hallucinatory images in real time, exploring nonhuman and machine cognition.

exhibitions.title: Iris van Herpen: Sculpting the Senses
exhibitions.description: North American debut of Dutch couturier Iris van Herpen, with 140+ sculptural haute couture creations shown alongside contemporary art, design, and natural history specimens.
exhibitions.venue_address: 200 Eastern Parkway, Brooklyn, NY 11238, United States

exhibitions.title: Yoshitomo Nara
exhibitions.description: New paintings and drawings, recent sculptures, and early works spanning from the 1980s to today: the artist's first solo presentation with David Zwirner and his first major New York solo show in nearly a decade.

exhibitions.title: Brice Marden: I Am Plane Image
exhibitions.description: A comprehensive survey of Brice Marden's paintings spanning six decades at the West 21st Street gallery, the first such show of his work in New York in twenty years, with major loans from the Art Institute of Chicago, the Whitney, and other collections.

exhibitions.title: Jem Perucchini: Sospiro
exhibitions.description: New figurative paintings by Italian, Ethiopian-born Jem Perucchini (b. 1995), drawing on Renaissance painting, African wax prints and Ethiopian church frescoes. His first US exhibition.

exhibitions.title: Li Hei Di: the year of mud
exhibitions.description: New paintings by London-based Li Hei Di, between figuration and abstraction, shaped by the myth of the goddess Nüwa shaping people from mud. Their first solo show with Pace in New York.

exhibitions.title: Bea Scaccia: Groomed
exhibitions.description: Bea Scaccia's debut exhibition with the gallery, at the Park & 75 space: seven new paintings of nocturnal, sumptuous scenes assembled from fabric, wigs, jewelry and other accoutrements of feminine style, curated by Francesco Bonami.

exhibitions.title: David Byrne: Stairwell Drawings
exhibitions.description: Nine life-size drawings by Talking Heads' David Byrne line the stairwell landings between the flagship's first and seventh floors, reflecting his surreal, playful sensibility.

exhibitions.title: Architects of Liberation: Modernism in Western Africa
exhibitions.description: The first major survey of modern architecture across seven West African nations from the late 1950s to the early 1980s, exploring how building shaped newly independent states. Most objects have never been shown publicly.

exhibitions.title: Tone
exhibitions.description: A group show of nineteen artists, including Roy DeCarava, Kerry James Marshall and Lorna Simpson, exploring tone, from black to white and every value between, as an expressive material language.

exhibitions.title: A Sustained Becoming: Studio Museum Artists in Residence 2026
exhibitions.description: The first Artist-in-Residence cohort in the Studio Museum's new building: Derriann Pharr, Simonette Quamina and Taylor Simmons use figuration across mediums to explore cultural memory and time.

exhibitions.title: Focus Gallery: Oded Halahmy: Models in Wood
Isamu Noguchi: “I am not a designer”
Arthur Jafa: I Am Tony
exhibitions.description: Jafa's inaugural US museum survey spans nearly four decades of work, including "Love is the Message, The Message is Death" and the Golden Lion-winning "The White Album," alongside new pieces exploring Black life in America.
exhibitions.venue_address: 235 Bowery, New York, NY 10002, United States

exhibitions.title: There Are No Words: Si Lewen's Parade
exhibitions.description: Conceived by Si Lewen (1918–2016) in the aftermath of World War II, The Parade is informed by the artist's extraordinary life.

exhibitions.title: Guggenheim Pop: 1960 to Now
exhibitions.description: A sweeping survey of Pop art from the 1960s to today, with works by Warhol, Lichtenstein, Oldenburg, Hamilton and Chryssa shown alongside a Yayoi Kusama Infinity Mirror Room and recent contemporary acquisitions.
exhibitions.venue_address: 1071 Fifth Avenue, New York, NY 10128, United States

exhibitions.title: The Lost World: The Art of Minnie Evans
exhibitions.description: A touring retrospective of self-taught artist Minnie Evans's work from 1935-1981: vibrant drawings, paintings and collages blending spiritual imagery with natural motifs, made in North Carolina during the Jim Crow era.

exhibitions.title: Collection in Focus: Modern European Currents
exhibitions.description: Early 20th-century European avant-garde painting drawn from the collection, with works by Kandinsky, Goncharova, Franz Marc and others who reimagined painting for a rapidly changing world.
exhibitions.venue_address: 1071 Fifth Avenue, New York, NY 10128, United States

exhibitions.title: Costume Art
exhibitions.description: Inaugurating the new Conde Nast Galleries, the Costume Institute pairs nearly 400 garments with paintings and sculpture to explore how art has depicted the dressed body.

exhibitions.title: Noguchi to Asawa: Designing Postwar America
I'm So Happy You Are Here: Japanese Women Photographers from the 1950s to Now
Laia Abril: On Rape and Institutional Failure
Melissa Ann Pinney: "What's Ms. Pinney Doing Here?"
David Lamelas: The Machine
exhibitions.description: A comprehensive survey of Argentine Conceptual artist David Lamelas, tracing his work from 1965 to today across film, sculpture and performance, unfolding as exhibition, film program and live work.

exhibitions.title: Zeng Fanzhi
exhibitions.description: Zeng Fanzhi's first New York exhibition in over a decade: a new sculpture and a suite of new paintings of imagined celestial landscapes, at the 22nd Street gallery.

exhibitions.title: Elmgreen & Dragset: TRANSITION
exhibitions.description: Elmgreen & Dragset debut a 40-ton, traversable steel sculpture with a new series of wall works, on the performative side of architecture. At Pace's 508 and 510 West 25th Street spaces.

exhibitions.title: Coumba Samba: Stars and Stripes
exhibitions.description: The inaugural solo museum presentation of Senegalese American artist Coumba Samba, an immersive installation examining nuclear power and African resource extraction through symbols of the U.S. military-industrial complex.

exhibitions.title: Siena: The Art of Bronze, 1450-1500
exhibitions.description: Nearly forty Renaissance bronzes, including works by Donatello and Francesco di Giorgio Martini, exploring the innovations of Sienese sculptors in the second half of the 15th century.

exhibitions.title: Gingerbread NYC
exhibitions.venue: Museum of the City of New York

exhibitions.title: The Surrealist Book: Tomorrow Lives in Mirrors
exhibitions.description: A survey of Surrealism's book-as-art-object experiments by André Breton, Salvador Dalí, Claude Cahun, Max Ernst and others, built around a major gift of rare artists' books from the Helen and Sam Zell Collection.

exhibitions.title: Lucas Samaras: Boxes and Reconstructions
exhibitions.description: Lucas Samaras's box sculptures of the 1960s to 1980s alongside never-before-seen fabric paintings from his 1979 Reconstructions series.

exhibitions.title: Form, Shadow, Motion: Selections from the Burger Collection, Hong Kong
Hyundai Translocal Series: Ho Tzu Nyen
exhibitions.description: A new site-specific video work by Singapore-based artist Ho Tzu Nyen installed in the museum's OMA-designed elevators, part of an ongoing series exploring power, endurance, and transformation.
exhibitions.venue_address: 235 Bowery, New York, NY 10002, United States

exhibitions.title: Screens Series: Umi Ishihara
exhibitions.description: The US institutional debut of London- and Tokyo-based artist Umi Ishihara, bringing together three recent films exploring precarity and collective life through personal memory and social realities.
exhibitions.venue_address: 235 Bowery, New York, NY 10002, United States

exhibitions.title: Through Motion and Repose: Expanding the Walls 2026
exhibitions.description: Photography by seventeen teen artists from the Studio Museum's signature Expanding the Walls program, capturing New York's streets alongside intimate moments at home.

exhibitions.title: Geometries
exhibitions.description: A group exhibition exploring geometry as an organizational principle, translating sources from city maps to West African textiles into a shared visual vocabulary spanning figuration and abstraction.

exhibitions.title: Krasner and Pollock: Past Continuous
exhibitions.description: The first major New York presentation devoted to either artist in more than 20 years.

exhibitions.title: Art of Manga
exhibitions.description: East Coast debut of the first major Americas exhibition on manga as an art form, with more than 600 original drawings including Inuyasha, JoJo's Bizarre Adventure and ONE PIECE.
exhibitions.venue_address: 200 Eastern Parkway, Brooklyn, NY 11238, United States

exhibitions.title: Manga Before Manga: Japanese Art from the Collection
exhibitions.description: Twenty-one works from the collection trace 900 years of Japanese narrative imagery behind modern manga; a companion to Art of Manga.
exhibitions.venue_address: 200 Eastern Parkway, Brooklyn, NY 11238, United States

exhibitions.title: The Bowery: Devil's Mile
exhibitions.description: The inaugural exhibition traces five centuries of the Bowery's history, from Lenape footpath through skid row to thriving arts community, examining the street as a site of ongoing reinvention.
exhibitions.venue_address: 235 Bowery, New York, NY 10002, United States

exhibitions.title: Diego Marcon: Arrivederci, Piggies!
exhibitions.description: The Italian artist's first solo New York museum show presents three recent films alongside the newly commissioned "Krapfen" (2025), blending horror, comedy, and animation to explore desire, memory, and perception.
exhibitions.venue_address: 235 Bowery, New York, NY 10002, United States

exhibitions.title: Designing the Gilded Age: Drawings from the Studios of Louis C. Tiffany
exhibitions.description: The dazzling stained-glass windows, lamps, mosaics, and interiors from Tiffany's studios began as drawings created by the many talented designers who worked there.

exhibitions.title: Breaking the Mold: Brooklyn Museum at 200
exhibitions.description: Three chapters of longtime favorites and new standouts, bringing fresh narratives to the fore while exploring the collection's history and future evolution. Marks the Museum's bicentennial.
exhibitions.venue_address: 200 Eastern Parkway, Brooklyn, NY 11238, United States

exhibitions.title: David Hartt: Peripheries
exhibitions.description: Multidisciplinary artist David Hartt transforms John Vanderlyn's 19th-century painting Panoramic View of the Palace and Gardens of Versailles into a site-specific installation exploring place and perspective.

exhibitions.title: Sacred Splendor: Jewish Ritual Art and Christian Treasures from St. Vitus Cathedral in Prague
Focus Gallery: Hannah Altman: Not a Circle but a Spiral
Focus Gallery: Afruz Amighi: Sounding Shell
Teresa Margolles

exhibitions.venue_address: 22-25 Jackson Avenue, Long Island City, NY 11101

exhibitions.title: Homeroom: Artists Against the Bomb
exhibitions.description: An international artistic campaign in support of the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons, presenting posters, film, photography, sculpture and ephemera by artists including Regina José Galindo and Carlos Amorales, organized by Estudio Pedro Reyes and ICAN.
exhibitions.venue_address: 22-25 Jackson Avenue, Long Island City, NY 11101

exhibitions.title: Frederic Church in Jamaica
exhibitions.description: Over 60 oil and graphite sketches from Church's 1865 trip to Jamaica, documenting plant life and landscapes, drawn from Cooper Hewitt's collection of the artist's work.

exhibitions.title: The Substitute
exhibitions.description: Alexandra Daisy Ginsberg's immersive video and sound installation digitally resurrects an extinct male Northern white rhino using AI and visual effects, questioning whether species resurrection is a justified answer to extinction.

exhibitions.title: Brancusi: The Artist and His Studio
exhibitions.description: For the first time in decades, rarely lent sculptures leave Brancusi's Paris atelier (closed for renovation) to join MoMA's Brancusi collection, alongside his photographs, films, hand-carved furniture, tools and archival materials.

exhibitions.title: Dreams of This Future: The Collection of Peggy Cooper Cafritz
exhibitions.description: The first exhibition to tell the story of arts advocate Peggy Cooper Cafritz as a collector, drawing on her bequest of over 200 artists of African descent across multiple media.

exhibitions.title: Jakob Kudsk Steensen: Wetland
exhibitions.description: Digital installation Berl-Berl reimagines Berlin's lost wetlands as a singing, digital swamp, blending ecological research, Slavic folklore and game-engine technology to explore human and more-than-human worlds.

exhibitions.title: Taryn Simon | Father Country I Do Love You
exhibitions.description: A major new commission premieres never-before-seen photographs, text, video, and sculpture in a single interactive installation spiraling through the entire rotunda.
exhibitions.venue_address: 1071 Fifth Avenue, New York, NY 10128, United States

exhibitions.title: New York Fashion at PS1, 1980–1984
exhibitions.description: Archive material and partial reconstructions of the fashion installations curator Hollywood Di Russo staged at PS1 with Julio, Charles James, Willi Smith and Betsey Johnson.
exhibitions.venue_address: 22-25 Jackson Avenue, Long Island City, NY 11101

exhibitions.title: Hard Art
exhibitions.description: A major exhibition examining the legacy of abstract painting by Black artists in the US from 1969 to today, featuring over forty artists across three generations.
exhibitions.venue_address: 22-25 Jackson Avenue, Long Island City, NY 11101

exhibitions.title: Masao Gozu: Windows and Bars
exhibitions.description: First US museum show of Masao Gozu: photographs from the 1970s to today, from his Windows series of tenement residents and the Harry's Bar series, with recent returns to the same sites.
exhibitions.venue_address: 22-25 Jackson Avenue, Long Island City, NY 11101

exhibitions.title: The Occupied City
exhibitions.venue: Museum of the City of New York

exhibitions.title: Kapwani Kiwanga: BLEED
exhibitions.description: A site-specific installation by Kapwani Kiwanga reworking the quilting "flying geese" pattern in natural dyes, evoking the Underground Railroad and histories of Black resistance.

exhibitions.title: Donald Moffett: IMPEACH
exhibitions.description: An immersive sound installation built around Representative John Lewis's speech on the floor of the US House during the December 1998 impeachment debate.
exhibitions.venue_address: 200 Eastern Parkway, Brooklyn, NY 11238, United States

exhibitions.title: Cézanne to Modigliani: Gifts of Modern Art from the Pearlman Collection
exhibitions.description: More than 50 modern European works by Cézanne, Modigliani, Degas, Gauguin, Toulouse-Lautrec and Soutine, from the Henry and Rose Pearlman Collection gift.
exhibitions.venue_address: 200 Eastern Parkway, Brooklyn, NY 11238, United States

exhibitions.title: Halumii Ktapihna
exhibitions.venue: Museum of the City of New York

exhibitions.title: Taking Back Our Space: Photographic Perspectives
exhibitions.description: Marianne Wex's 1970s feminist photo survey of gendered body language is shown alongside contemporary artists Nona Faustine, Martine Gutierrez, K8 Hardy, Yuki Kihara, Joiri Minaya, Paulina Olowska, and Wendy Red Star, reappraising bodies in public space.

exhibitions.title: Light and Stone: Revisiting Noguchi’s 1986 Venice Biennale
Roy Lichtenstein: Like New
exhibitions.description: A comprehensive retrospective of roughly 130 works spanning the 1940s through the 1990s, tracing how Roy Lichtenstein transformed mass-culture imagery into iconic Pop art while probing duplication and the circulation of images across media.

exhibitions.title: Graphic Devotions: Late Medieval European Blockbooks
exhibitions.description: Blockbooks from 1450–80, when woodblock-printed books competed with manuscripts and typeset books, including a rare Ars moriendi, from the largest US collection of blockbooks.

exhibitions.title: Flip Sides: Seeing Korean Art Anew
exhibitions.description: Treasured Korean objects are turned around to reveal their interiors, reverses, and hidden details, offering a fuller view of each work's form across two rotations.

exhibitions.title: Roy Lichtenstein: 1997
exhibitions.description: A focused show of rarely seen works from the final year of the Pop artist's life, including prints, photographs and sculptural maquettes alongside studies for unrealized projects, revealing his late-career experimentation.

exhibitions.title: Michael Richards: Free F’All
exhibitions.description: Michael Richards's sculpture of a pilot pierced with nails commemorates the Tuskegee Airmen, the US Air Force's first Black unit.
exhibitions.venue_address: 200 Eastern Parkway, Brooklyn, NY 11238, United States

exhibitions.title: The Genesis Facade Commission: Liu Wei, Speculation
exhibitions.description: Beijing-based artist Liu Wei (born 1972) inspires visitors to ponder cycles of rupture and resistance for the 2026 Genesis Facade Commission.

exhibitions.title: Full Disclosure: The Edge of Information Design
exhibitions.description: MoMA's first exhibition devoted entirely to information design, presenting 30 works of digital and analog design (including six new acquisitions) that explore how designers help visualize and shape our understanding of complex data.

exhibitions.title: Nilima Sheikh: Fractured Skies
exhibitions.description: A survey of painter Nilima Sheikh's five-decade practice, tracing her engagement with Kashmir through narrative scroll paintings including a new, site-responsive series debuting at MoMA.

exhibitions.title: Hopi Kachina Dolls: Blessings for a Balanced World
exhibitions.description: The first exhibition to examine the Hopi kachina doll tradition from the perspective of the women and girls who receive them, presented at the Center for Feminist Art.
exhibitions.venue_address: 200 Eastern Parkway, Brooklyn, NY 11238, United States

exhibitions.title: Tapa: Art of the Gift in Polynesia
exhibitions.description: 19th-century bark cloth tapa from Fiji, Samoa and Futuna, plus a Niuean hiapo on loan from Te Papa, shown as ceremonial gifts and diplomacy. Gallery 359.

exhibitions.title: Rediscovering Della Robbia at The Met
exhibitions.description: Results from a collaborative exchange among curators, conservators, and digital specialists studying The Met's Della Robbia sculptures.

exhibitions.title: Our Flag Was Still There
exhibitions.description: Historic American flags tied to 9/11, including the Ground Zero Flag, paired with personal stories in Foundation Hall to mark the nation's 250th anniversary.
exhibitions.venue_address: 180 Greenwich Street, New York, NY 10007, United States

exhibitions.title: Responding in Ink: Comic Books, Graphic Novels, and 9/11
exhibitions.description: Examines how comic book and graphic novel artists responded to 9/11, from pre-2001 fictional depictions of the World Trade Center through decades of memoirs, charitable efforts, and educational works.
exhibitions.venue_address: 180 Greenwich Street, New York, NY 10007, United States

exhibitions.title: A King's Carpet: Louis XIV and the Savonnerie
exhibitions.description: The first US exhibition on the Savonnerie centers The Met's three monumental Baroque carpets woven for Louis XIV's Grande Galerie at the Louvre, tracing their making and dispersal.

exhibitions.title: In Their Honor: 25 Years of 9/11-Inspired Service
exhibitions.description: Opened for the 25th anniversary, this exhibition explores how individuals and communities transformed grief into service inspired by 9/11, among a generation with no lived memory of the attacks.
exhibitions.venue_address: 180 Greenwich Street, New York, NY 10007, United States

exhibitions.title: Rubin Museum Tibetan Buddhist Shrine Room
exhibitions.description: A six-year installation of the Rubin Museum's beloved Tibetan Buddhist Shrine Room within the Arts of Asia galleries: over 100 thangkas, sculptures, and ritual objects arranged as an elaborate household shrine, with chanted prayers, butter lamps, and incense.
exhibitions.venue_address: 200 Eastern Parkway, Brooklyn, NY 11238, United States

exhibitions.title: Charles Burchfield: Elemental
exhibitions.description: Ten watercolors from the Whitney's collection, spanning 1916–1960, tracing Charles Burchfield's visionary, lifelong reverence for natural phenomena, from flowering meadows to dramatic storms.

exhibitions.title: Design Across Time: Exploring the Smithsonian’s Design Collection
Raise Your Voice
exhibitions.venue: Museum of the City of New York

exhibitions.title: Julie Curtiss: UNREAL
exhibitions.description: New paintings by Julie Curtiss of faceless figures in New York apartments, laundromats and bodegas, in her first presentation with Gagosian in New York, at 541 West 24th Street.

exhibitions.title: A Long Shadow: Postwar Japan Through the Lens
exhibitions.description: Postwar Japanese photography, from Okinawa and base towns under US occupation, drawn from the Met's collection with rare photobooks and new acquisitions. Gallery 851.

exhibitions.title: Kent Monkman: Officer and Laughing Girl
exhibitions.description: New paintings by contemporary artist Kent Monkman responding to Vermeer's Officer and Laughing Girl, examining trade, colonization and Indigenous-European encounters through his alter ego Miss Chief.

exhibitions.title: Georg Baselitz: Meine Schule
exhibitions.description: Georg Baselitz's last completed paintings and sculptures, curated by Richard Calvocoressi, at 555 West 24th Street; the gallery's first Baselitz show since his death in April.

exhibitions.title: 25th Anniversary Exhibition: Masterworks from the Neue Galerie
exhibitions.description: Opening Autumn 2026, this milestone show fills the entire museum with collection highlights, from Klimt's Adele Bloch-Bauer I to German and Austrian masterworks and Wiener Werkstaette design.

exhibitions.title: Ragtime: Cakewalk in Pianoland
exhibitions.description: Early printed ragtime and cakewalk music from the John Davis Collection of Early Printed Musical African Americana, setting Ernest Hogan beside Scott Joplin.

exhibitions.title: Rothko/Gottlieb: The Surrealist Years
exhibitions.description: Paintings and works on paper by Mark Rothko and Adolph Gottlieb from 1941 to 1951, when both turned to myth and Surrealist abstraction. Curated by Arne Glimcher.

exhibitions.title: Na Mira: NO SMOKING
exhibitions.description: Na Mira's first solo museum exhibition in New York: a newly commissioned media installation in the Kravis Studio using radio frequencies, infrared heat and holography, drawing on Korean shamanism and structural filmmaking.

exhibitions.title: The Nature of Color
exhibitions.description: An interactive exhibition on what color reveals about the natural world and ourselves, from how animals and plants use it to how it shapes mood.
exhibitions.venue_address: 200 Central Park West, New York, NY 10024, United States

exhibitions.title: Alex Webb: Walking Blues
exhibitions.description: Magnum photographer Alex Webb's bold-colour street pictures from some forty US cities, shaped by the rhythm of blues music over more than a decade.
exhibitions.venue_address: 380 Columbus Avenue at West 78th Street, New York, NY 10024

exhibitions.title: The Photography Triennial: After Dark
exhibitions.venue: Museum of the City of New York

exhibitions.title: artport: A History of Internet Art
exhibitions.description: Marking the 25th anniversary of the Whitney's artport platform, this show gathers over 100 commissioned net-art works charting the evolution of internet art from 2001 to 2024.

exhibitions.title: Imitation of Life
exhibitions.description: World premiere musical with a book by Lynn Nottage and music and lyrics by John Legend, directed by Liesl Tommy. Two mothers, one Black and one White, raise their daughters across 1920s Atlantic City and 1930s New York.

exhibitions.title: Éliane Radigue: States of Listening
exhibitions.description: Co-organized with Blank Forms, this show restages French composer Éliane Radigue's pulsating 1970s sonic installations in Dia's program space, with live synthesizer and acoustic performances.

exhibitions.title: Virgil Abloh: The Codes
exhibitions.description: A survey of Virgil Abloh's work in fashion, art, architecture and music: nearly 1,000 objects from his archive over 28,000 sq ft, including a recreation of his Paris office.

exhibitions.title: Across Wine-Dark Seas: Art and Identity beyond Ancient Greece
exhibitions.description: Presents more than 180 exceptional works exploring art and identity beyond ancient Greece.

exhibitions.title: Austrian Masterworks from the Neue Galerie
Farah Al Qasimi: TAILSPIN
exhibitions.description: A video exhibition exploring American industry, oil culture and Arab immigration through the perspective of a jinn, blending documentary footage and personal testimony to examine identity in post-9/11 America.

exhibitions.title: Sixth New Museum Triennial: The Outside Expands
exhibitions.description: The sixth edition of the museum's signature international triennial for early-career artists, co-curated by Vivian Crockett and Isabella Rjeille, examines how artists destabilize fixed notions of territory, identity, gender, and sexuality.
exhibitions.venue_address: 235 Bowery, New York, NY 10002, United States

exhibitions.title: Sonya Kelliher-Combs: TITIQ/MARK
exhibitions.description: Nearly two decades of work by Iñupiaq and Koyukon artist Sonya Kelliher-Combs (paintings, sculptures and installations on history, cultural continuity and land use), her first solo museum show in New York.

exhibitions.title: Woody De Othello: coming forth by day
exhibitions.description: Miami-born Woody De Othello's new ceramic and wood sculptures, tiled wall works and a large bronze, his first institutional solo show in New York, travelling from Pérez Art Museum Miami.

exhibitions.title: William Blake: Paradise Lost
exhibitions.description: For the 200th anniversary of Blake's death, his Milton-inspired watercolors, illuminated books and paintings reunited, with works by Fuseli and Flaxman.

exhibitions.title: The City Electric
exhibitions.venue: Museum of the City of New York
